messages:
IncBot: :rotating_light: PAGER: GPU autoscaler for cluster-prod hit max_nodes ceiling. queue_len spike detected for route=\"/v1/generate\". initiating incident channel. Pager: alex (on-call).

alex (on-call): seeing it, joining. what's the current max_nodes and target pool?

maya: gpu-serve pool is at max_nodes=100 (policy hard cap). Pending pods ~ 24, ready nodes 100, cpu/gpu utilization 96%. queue backlog growth +1200/s over 5m. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/boards/rl-gpu-pool?from=now-15m

chris: confirmed. autoscaler attempted scale to 120 but rejected by pool ceiling. kubectl describe shows pods Pending because "Insufficient nodes".

kevin: any recent deploys or traffic change? traffic spike looks real — one customer ran a large embedding job. CS says they kicked off batch for 3 tenants. @customer-success can you confirm which customers?

customer-success: affected: "AcmeRetail", "DriftAnalytics". both reported slow responses and some 429s from our API. ETA on mitigation?

alex (on-call): Triage plan: 1) try one-time manual cap bump to 130, 2) if cloud quota blocks, provision emergency fallback: route low-priority workloads to dedicated-fallback-model, 3) notify impacted customers. Who can do the cap bump? Need IAM with infra-admin.

maya: I can request override but need finance/infra approval for temporary commit increase. Trying infra-cli now:
```
$ infra-cli pool update --name gpu-serve --max-nodes 130
Updating pool gpu-serve...
Error: quota_exceeded: requested 30 additional GPUs, but account quota is 20. Request a quota increase: /infra/quotas/requests
```

chris: hitting cloud quota. I'll try manual cloud console request under the billing project; sometimes immediate if approved. Opening support ticket with cloud: INC-99823.

sysops-bot: support ticket INC-99823 created against cloud-provider for quota increase (priority=P1). Link: https://cloudprovider/support/INC-99823

alex (on-call): while cloud handles quota, please move non-critical pods off gpu-serve: apply label "priority=low" -> move to burst-pool. Use pod evict + nodeSelector change.

maya: starting eviction for pods with label app=evals,priority=low. Command:
```
kubectl get pods -l app=evals,priority=low -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete --grace-period=30
```
Will monitor backlog after evictions.

kevin: routing change applied. /v1/generate route now has weight 80% gpu-serve, 20% fallback. config snippet:
```json
{"routes": [{"path":"/v1/generate","pool":"gpu-serve","weight":0.8},{"path":"/v1/generate","pool":"gpu-fallback","weight":0.2} ]}
```

chris: cloud support responded: can increase quota but requires manual acceptance from billing owner. pinging @maya_billing (external). If we get approval within 10m, we can bump to 140.

maya: billing approved one-time increase to 130. Proceeding to update pool via cloud console now.

chris: done. cloud shows nodes provisioning, expected ready ~6-8 minutes. New target max_nodes=130 applied.

IncBot: Node pool gpu-serve scaling events: +12 nodes initiated. Estimated add time 7m.

alex (on-call): monitoring queues. backlog growth stopped and started to decrease. 5m avg latency dropping. Good sign.

customer-success: notifying impacted customers with short blurb and ETA for full recovery, cc support.

kevin: after nodes ready, reconcile pending pods. kubectl get pods shows Pending -> Running. Throughput back to normal.

maya: metrics look healthy: GPU util ~82%, queue_len trending to baseline. No further 429s reported from customers.

alex (on-call): mitigation complete. Next steps: 1) follow up with infra to request permanent pool ceiling review, 2) create post-incident eval for batching policies and customer throttle protections, 3) schedule runbook update to include quick cloud-billing approval flow.

chris: creating incident ticket and will attach logs + CLI commands: INC-2026-03-09-gpu-ceil-bump.

sysops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-09-gpu-ceil-bump. Owner: chris.

alex (on-call): Handoff to oncall-next for monitoring through next 2 hours. @kevin please watch dashboards.

kevin: watching. will escalate if any regression. :thumbsup:

customer-success: sent follow-up messages to AcmeRetail and DriftAnalytics with apologies and compensation offer.

maya: temporary manual cap will be reverted to policy after stability window. I'll file a PR to adjust pool policy (proposal: soft cap at 120, hard cap at 200 with billing approval flows).

alex (on-call): thanks all. Incident status -> resolved. Will add postmortem notes and link here when ready. :white_check_mark:
